narrative:
The model estimated a 27.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning roughly a one-in-four chance of serious repayment difficulty based on your profile. Under the lender’s policy, that score fell into the denied range, so the application was not approved.

The strongest influences on this decision were the requested loan amount, your length of employment, and your installment rate. Importantly, all three worked in your favor by lowering the estimated risk. Your requested amount of 3,001 DM is very close to the approved-applicant average of about 3,020 DM, so it was not an excessive request. Your employment history of four to seven years is reasonably stable and supported a lower-risk view. Your installment rate of 2% of disposable income is below the approved average of about 2.99%, also a favorable sign.

Because these leading factors pushed toward good credit, the denial was not driven by them. Rather, the combined effect of less influential details in your profile left the overall risk estimate at 27.0%, still above the approval cutoff. This does not mean default is certain; it means the lender’s policy treated the overall profile as too risky at this time. You should ask the lender for a detailed explanation, check that your data is accurate, and consider strengthening the application—for example by building savings, adding a suitable guarantor or co-applicant, or reapplying after your financial position improves.
